coursesExamined.name: Personal & Professional Development
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
coursesExamined.contribution: Required personal/academic development, research literacy and civic engagement.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. coursesExamined.name: Consumer Product Design
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one. Students investigate product mechanisms and environmental impact, interview potential customers, translate needs into specifications, select concepts, and develop production plans and prototypes where feasible. The final project integrates these stages with industrial scaling and elementary economic analysis. Sustainability, including material use, repairability, lifespan and circularity, informs design decisions throughout.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops product mechanisms, user needs/specifications, concept selection, prototyping and production plans with sustainability and industrial scaling. Genuine design methods; no assumed electronic-system or circuit design assignment.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

coursesExamined.name: Decision-making in AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops the mathematical foundations of intelligent-agent decisions under uncertainty. Probability and Bayesian networks support belief updating and inference, while temporal models address changing environments. Decision theory, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems connect uncertainty to policies and expected utility. Multi-agent decisions introduce strategic and collective interaction, and probabilistic programming provides a framework for expressing models. Students work through equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
coursesExamined.contribution: models planning with uncertainty, partial observability and resource constraints for autonomous computational agents
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

coursesExamined.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces formal logic, abstract mathematical reasoning and proof. Students analyze propositions and quantified statements, work with sets, Boolean algebra, functions and relations, and develop direct and indirect proofs. Induction and recursive definitions extend these tools to mathematical structures. The final component systematically models processes and games without chance and investigates the existence and construction of winning strategies.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops logic and discrete structures for algorithm construction and reasoning about computational systems, without claiming digital-circuit design
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.

coursesExamined.name: Optimization Methods in AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies search and optimization for rational agents in known, complex and adversarial environments. Students move from uninformed and heuristic search to local and global optimization, first- and second-order methods and population approaches. Adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimization extend the toolkit. Laboratories and projects require algorithm tracing, implementation and evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Covers computational methods for search problems in complex and adversarial environments. Includes uninformed and informed search, local and global search, adversarial games and constraint satisfaction problems.
coursesExamined.contribution: implements search, local/global methods and constraint satisfaction for complex computational decision problems
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.

coursesExamined.name: Networks & Operating Systems
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies computer networks and operating systems as the infrastructure for communication and resource management. Internet protocols are examined through the application, transport, network and link layers. Operating-system study covers processes, threads, scheduling, concurrency, memory and persistent storage. Wireshark laboratories and investigative projects connect these concepts to observed packet behaviour, network properties and experimental examination of operating-system performance.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces computer networks and operating systems. Covers how the internet works and the role of an OS in resource management and application support.
coursesExamined.contribution: studies computer networks, internet operation and operating-system resource management, directly supporting the communication-network strand rather than analogue communication physics
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Introduces computer networks and operating systems. Covers how the internet works and the role of an OS in resource management and application support.

coursesExamined.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies algorithm design and analysis, emphasizing how algorithms and data structures affect execution time. Students examine sorting, searching, random-number generation, string matching and graph algorithms, then study computability, verification, reductions and complexity classes. Programming and mathematical exercises develop algorithmic understanding, while projects require students to design, execute and report experimental investigations of performance.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Teaches design and analysis of algorithms and data structures, emphasizing performance analysis and focusing on prominent algorithms and data structures.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops and analyses algorithms and data structures for efficient computational systems

coursesExamined.name: Advanced Algorithms
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies algebraic algorithms and advanced optimization methods through mathematical reasoning, implementation and experimental analysis. Fast and exact arithmetic, number-theoretic algorithms, matrix multiplication and Fourier transformation lead into hashing, greedy methods, dynamic programming and network flows. Laboratories develop algorithmic understanding, while projects investigate exact computing and optimization, including hypotheses, measured performance and sensitivity analysis.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Studies modern algebraic algorithms and optimization methods. Emphasises algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling of computational problems.
coursesExamined.contribution: extends mathematical modelling and algorithm design to algebraic and optimisation problems
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Studies modern algebraic algorithms and optimization methods. Emphasises algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling of computational problems.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Data Science

Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops data preparation, visualisation and manipulation for computational-system investigations; its spatial and text datasets are methods examples rather than electrical measurements

coursesExamined.name: Machine Learning

Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.

Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.

academicJudgment: Linear Systems genuinely develops transforms,filtering,modulation andfeedback; Robotics programs a physical arm andgripper; Energy&Sustainability examines grids/storage/mini-grids; RenewableSystemDesign assesses technical/economic energy options; ConsumerProductDesign provides actual specifications,concepts andprototypes. These are not dismissed as generic context. The full candidate nevertheless organises most learning around mathematical/computational agents,data/algorithm work andenergy appraisal. It does not integrate electrical/semiconductor behaviour,circuit analysis anddevice-level measurements into a sustained progression of electrical-system analysis,design andtesting,which the target learning outcomes andprojects make central. Missing some Delft courses would not itself justify rejection; the absent organising physical-electrical inquiry after strengthening does. No degree-title,licence,exact-equivalence ormatching-course quota is imposed.
otherCandidates: The medical/neuroscience option supplies genuine biological questions,neural signalling andcognitive experiments,but not physiological-instrument/device electronic design. It would rename neuroscience/computation as medical electronics. A circuits/chips/electromagnetics concept has no sustained device-analysis/design implementation in current active coursework. No accepted later alternative follows a rejected closest response.
alignmentFinding: The previous mathematical/signal/network correspondences are genuine partial relationships, not proof of whole-programme comparability. All original positive alignments are preserved in the archived decision and retired from the active comparison.
